analysis:
Examined the complete supplied documentation patch and BASE surrounding release, signing, publication, recovery, identity and rollback procedures. docs/operations/provider-release.md HEAD 265–309 replaces master dev publication with a dev-branch lane, documents master-owned source verification and environment guards, and states that dev artifacts now satisfy the production updater's Apple/team requirement. HEAD 503–573 replaces secret-free ad-hoc branch signing with shared Developer ID signing/notarization and inherited repository secrets; it also explicitly says dev review is not currently enforced and requires a pull-request rule before activation. These changes affect the contracts for A-005, A-011, A-017, TB-003, TB-010, TB-011 and T-054; artifact signatures alone must not become production serving authorization (T-052/T-056).
No independently supported executable regression is established by this documentation-only source scope. Integration must inspect .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml, scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py and resolve-provider-release.sh to verify which revision supplies secret-bearing scripts, exact dev ancestry/signature checks, environment confinement and whether activation is blocked pending the documented review prerequisite. Confirm that production registration/qualification still excludes dev artifacts despite shared signing identity; do not infer this from the signature or documentation alone. The documented non-SemVer latest-release collision at HEAD 551–570 also needs reconciliation with publication waiting/alias logic and the actual platform contract; links do not establish deployment. BASE prerequisites at 131–149 still describe dev sources as trusted master and should be reconciled with the new dev gate. No request encryption, plaintext handling, billing or native inference changes are supplied here.
